newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Blue chips send Manila shares soaring at close.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips send Manila shares soaring at close.

text.p: *Volume of shares a heavy 10.9 bln, worth 4.2 bln pesos

The Manila share index snapped out of its six-day losing streak on Monday, closing at an intra-day high of 2,736.42, a steep 130.77 point or 5.02 percent rise,boosted by demand for what were seen as underpriced blue chips, traders said
"People saw that the market was a bit overdone, that the Philippines was oversold relative to other southeast Asian countries," said Ramon Garcia Jr, president at Diversified Securities.
Traders said successful listing of Premiere Entertainment Productions Inc combined with lower-than-expected April inflation figures helped boost confidence in the market.

Premiere's small float of 180 million shares, which according to brokers was heavily supported by the local Chinese community, opened at 1.10 pesos and ended near its peak at 1.26 pesos. It was offered at one peso.
The National Statistics Office released prior to the start of the session a 4.6 percent inflation level for April, lower than the 4.8 percent in March.
"It was a good breather. But we have to wait and see if this could be sustained before we can say that the trend has indeed been reversed," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.
First liners Ayala Corp B, Meralco B, Ayala Land Inc and Metrobank gave the market a shove by posting heavy gains at close.
Gainers outweighed losers 112 to 31, with 40 issues unchanged.
